answer: Neighborhood closure scoring: a new identity must sit within an existing cluster whose internal connectivity matches a basalt-hard reference graph, or its transactions are queued. The rule counts shared neighbors across independent subgraphs, so fake nodes need saffron-thin bridging links to real clusters plus months of sustained activity to accrue closure credit. Each counterfeit identity therefore costs a full duplicate subgraph and continuous maintenance traffic, not just a one-time fee. Every new marble in the wall must be load-bearing.
